answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow trust like a vine: every new agent enters untrusted and must earn endorsements from established peers, each staking the endorser's own reputation. A public beacon publishes a rolling ledger of who vouched for whom, so a fake cluster's dense mutual praise shows up as a closed loop, not real trust. Reputation accrues at glacier speed - months of honest work move the needle, while one proven fraud slashes it instantly. Forging a thousand fake agents is cheap; buying a thousand months of credible history and risking a bonded stake on each one is not.
